review: Native memory film/export dismissal lifecycle repair candidate
status: Source frozen; focused checks passed; actual new iPhone/Android acceptance remains required.

evidence.observation: The e173 iPhone first failed Book settings visibility after successful film/export close and return to the book. Settings issued its audience read and later appears behind the capture-open-link prompt. This is evidence of a presentation/lifecycle problem, not proof of a unique cause. No keyboard step was reached.
evidence.candidateMechanism: Prior close handlers synchronously removed the native Modal subtree through parent callbacks. The repair lets the same iOS Modal receive visible=false and remain mounted until native onDismiss before invoking the parent handoff.

installedReactNative.semantics: iOS _shouldShowModal checks visible or internal isRendered; onDismiss clears isRendered and invokes the current callback. Android has no corresponding onDismiss guarantee and keeps immediate completion.

changes: Use a shared dismissal hook with one pending request ticket, synchronous close cleanup, native acknowledgement, and exactly-once completion.

Commit book/session visit identity in a layout effect. Unmount invalidates pending callbacks in layout cleanup. Recheck current navigationScope before dispatch and completion, including same-owner replacement and A-to-B-to-A session changes.
Use bookId plus existing navigation scope only. Do not cancel a legitimate close for new page-array objects, renewed media URLs, title/revision or export content-stamp refresh.

For post navigation, require the committed current items to retain the selected page/post association. Publish the existing Film event-state ref in a layout effect; stopForDismissal still immediately disallows playback.

Stop film playback and abort/release export at the close request. Guard export creation and Photos actions from a stale control after close. Late export results remain subject to existing cancellation/release ownership.
Preserve existing labels, native animation types, presentation style, media deadlines, export rights checks and feature flags. No new network work, global listeners or fallback timer.
Production MemoryAlbumScreen already keys Film by bookId:viewerId and unmounts when no pages remain. Do not retain removed/revoked page content or change that parent behavior.

counterexample.name: e173-negative
counterexample.method: A Node preload replaced only fs reads of the two production TSX files with git show e173b2db versions. Hook/test/harness and all other reads used current source. The two selected tests fail at immediate parent completion assertions. No working-tree source was replaced.
counterexample.selection: ^iOS (Close memory film pauses immediately|export cancellation aborts immediately)

coverage: iOS Close/Read/native-request transitions and subtree retention until acknowledged, including 30 seconds of virtual time with no substitute callback
Repeated control/native callbacks, unmount, same-owner session replacement and account ABA before a replacement render
Book replacement during dismissal, stale controls and old native acknowledgements; these are defensive shared-hook checks, while production Film also remounts by book/viewer key
Same-book page/delivery/presentation refresh without cancelling legitimate close; changed source suppresses stale onPost
Immediate export abort, ready-result release, late-result disposal and stale Photos guard
Android Close/Read/export immediate completion without onDismiss
Existing media readiness, looping, progress, playback pause/background/call boundaries, video terminal/deadline behavior and private media caching
testBoundaries: Actual MemoryFilm/MemoryMovieExport TSX and the actual dismissal hook execute. React hooks, native UI, UIKit acknowledgement, transport/encoder and Photos are controlled adapters.
No actual UIKit animation, GPU drawing, accessibility hierarchy or Photos permission dialog is exercised by the local component cases.
The controlled harness does not simulate abandoned concurrent React renders; committed-ref publication is source-reviewed.
These results establish ownership/state behavior and a regression against prior immediate callbacks. They do not prove the e173 native presentation failure is cured.

reactBestPracticesReview.result: No remaining issue within the changed scope after review.
findings: Interaction cleanup stays in event handlers, with refs for pending ownership and one state value for visible dismissal. No derived-state effect loop.
Layout effects only publish committed identities/event state or invalidate unmounted requests; they do not fetch, set routine derived state or delay native acknowledgement.
The visit memo retains a request-ownership identity for primitive book/session dependencies; ordinary content refresh cannot invalidate the handoff.
Direct imports, unchanged hooks order and explicit boolean predicate types. Full native TypeScript and exact-file ESLint pass.
No additional global listeners, network waterfalls or package dependencies. Existing accessibility labels and controls remain unchanged.
Web/server-only recommendations are inapplicable to these native components.

requiredNextGate: New complete iPhone and Android native runs must pass navigation through Book settings plus the separately mandatory actual-capture/encoding/readback/cleanup flow. Do not reduce assertions or timeouts.
